findings: Russian practical transcription is comparative only; Ukrainian output is not generated through Russian.
Project policy: Thai /h/ → Ukrainian г in the practical adapter; preserve typed IPA /h/ and allow sourced lexical exceptions for established Ukrainian exonyms.
Thai aspirates /kʰ pʰ tʰ tɕʰ/ use one Ukrainian practical letter each: к/п/т/ч; aspiration remains explicit in IPA and is not rendered as a second х.

Standard Thai /tɕ/ and /tɕʰ/ are voiceless alveolo-palatal affricates differing by aspiration, not voicing. Both map to practical ч; дж /d͡ʒ/ is inappropriate because it introduces voicing absent from the Thai phonemes.
Ч is a practical approximation, not exact IPA identity; the adapter must preserve IPA distinctions and document neutralized features.
Implementation now uses /h/ → г in both Python and browser IPA adapters; the generated consonant correspondence rows for ห/ฮ now show г.
Code inspection confirms the existing browser and Python adapters already implement the agreed mappings; this is not a new runtime accuracy improvement.
